paper.title: Reward Maximization Under Uncertainty: Leveraging Side-Observations on Networks

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic MAB with side-observations on a bipartite network (epsilon_t-greedy-LP)
unmapped: Feedback is given by a known bipartite graph between K actions and N base-arms: playing action j reveals samples of base-arms V_j; reward of action j is a known bounded function f_j of base-arms K_j subset of V_j
Base-arm samples independent across base-arms and i.i.d. over time
Algorithm needs the optimal solution z* of LP P2 (fractional hitting set of the graph)
settings.definition_quote: Let $\mathcal{N}=\{1,\ldots,N\}$ denote the collection of {\it base-arms} with unknown distributions. Subsets of base-arms form {\it actions}, and are indexed by $\mathcal{K}=\{1,\ldots,K\}$. ... When the decision maker chooses action $j$ at time $t$, he or she observes one realization for each of the random variables $X_i(t)$, $i\in V_j$. ... We assume that the reward is bounded in $[0,1]$ for each action.

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic MAB with side-observations on a bipartite network (UCB-LP, known horizon)
unmapped: Feedback given by a known bipartite graph between actions and base-arms; reward of action j is a known bounded function of base-arms K_j
Algorithm needs the optimal solution z* of LP P2
settings.definition_quote: When the decision maker chooses action $j$ at time $t$, he or she observes one realization for each of the random variables $X_i(t)$, $i\in V_j$. ... We assume that the reward is bounded in $[0,1]$ for each action.

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic MAB with side-observations on a bipartite network (UCB-LP, unknown horizon)
unmapped: Feedback given by a known bipartite graph between actions and base-arms; reward of action j is a known bounded function of base-arms K_j

settings.definition_quote: When the horizon is unknown, start the UCB-LP algorithm with $\tilde{T}_0=2$ and increase $\tilde{T}$ after reaching $\tilde{T}$ steps by setting $\tilde{T}_{l+1}=\tilde{T}_l^2.$

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic MAB with side-observations on a bipartite network (lower bound)
unmapped: Base-arm distributions from a one-parameter density family g(x;theta) satisfying Lai-Robbins finiteness, continuity and denseness assumptions
Feedback given by a known bipartite graph between actions and base-arms
settings.definition_quote: Let the probability distribution $F_{i}$ have a univariate density function $g(x;\theta_{i})$ with unknown parameters $\theta_{i}$, for each $i\in\mathcal{N}$.

symbols.c_bmu: optimal value of LP P1: min sum_{j suboptimal} Delta_j w_j s.t. sum_{j in S_i} w_j >= 1/J_i(theta_i) for all base-arms i, w >= 0

conditions: Assumptions 1-3 (finiteness, continuity, denseness of the KL/parametric family)

source.quote: Suppose Assumptions~\ref{eq:klcond1},~\ref{eq:klcond2}, and~\ref{eq:condo} hold. ... Then, under any uniformly good policy $\bm{\phi},$ the expected regret is asymptotically bounded below as follows: \liminf_{t\rightarrow\infty}\frac{R_{\bm{\mu}}(t)}{\log(t)}\ge c_{\bm{\mu}}, where $c_{\bm{\mu}}$ is the optimal value of the following linear program (LP) $P_{1}$

results.notes: Regret defined as sum Delta_j E[T_j(t)] (pseudo-regret). Derived by modifying Lai-Robbins Theorem 2. Renamed c_mu to c_bmu to avoid clash with canonical link-derivative symbol.

symbols.c_alg: exploration constant c of the policy
symbols.z_i: optimal solution of LP P2 (fractional hitting set) for action i

source.label: prop:epsgreedyk
source.quote: Choose parameters $c$ and $d$ such that, $0<d<\min_{j\in\cU}\Delta_{j}$, and $c>\max(2 \alpha d^{2}/r,4\alpha),$ for any $\alpha>1.$ Then, the expected regret at time $T$ of the $\epsilon_{t}$-greedy-LP policy ... is at most \left(\frac{c}{d^{2}}\sum_{j\in\cU}\Delta_{j}z_{j}^{*}\right)\log(T)+O(K), ... In particular, the $O(K)$ term is at most ...

results.notes: Derived from Proposition 7 (per-round probability of selecting a suboptimal action, not separately recorded). Policy is anytime. Remark 9 states order optimality under Assumption 4.

symbols.z_i: optimal solution of LP P2 for action i
symbols.b_i: indicator that suboptimal action i is in the set B = {j in U : m_j > m_bar}
symbols.Dhat_i: max{2^{-m_bar+2}, min_{a: i in G_a} Delta_a}

source.label: prop:ucblp
source.quote: Then, the expected regret due to the UCB-LP policy described in Algorithm~\ref{alg:ucblp} is at most \sum_{j\in \cU\setminus B} \Delta_{j} z_{j}^{*}\frac{32\log(T\hat{\Delta}_{j}^{2})}{\hat{\Delta}_{j}^{2}} + \sum_{j\in B} \frac{32\log(T\Delta_{j}^{2})}{\Delta_{j}}+O(K^{2}),

results.notes: Log terms have explicit constants; only the time-invariant O(K^2) term is asymptotic, hence notation O. Partial sums over U\B and B encoded with indicator b_i.

symbols.Z_star: optimal value sum_j z_j^* of LP P2

conditions: Assumption 4: |O|, min_j Delta_j and min_i J_i(theta_i) are constants independent of K and N

source.label: prop:ucblp
source.quote: Further, under Assumption~\ref{assum:bounded}, the regret is also at most O\left(\sum_{j\in\cK}z_{j}^{*}\log(T)\right) + O(K^{2}), where $(z_{j}^{*})$ entirely captures the time dependence on network structure.

results.notes: Hidden constant in the log term is 64/min Delta_j^2 per the proof.

source.label: app:unknown
source.quote: When the horizon is unknown, start the UCB-LP algorithm with $\tilde{T}_0=2$ and increase $\tilde{T}$ after reaching $\tilde{T}$ steps by setting $\tilde{T}_{l+1}=\tilde{T}_l^2.$ The regret of unknown horizon UCB-LP is bounded by \sum_{j\in \cU\setminus B}\frac{64\Delta_{j} z_{j}^{*}}{\hat{\Delta}_{j}^{2}} \log(T\hat{\Delta}_{j}^{2})+\sum_{j\in B} \frac{64\log(T\Delta_{j}^{2})}{\Delta_{j}}+O(K^2\log_2\log_2 T).

results.notes: log_2 log_2 T written as log(log(T)) up to constants inside O term.
